topic: Gruen sin-theta normal-offset shadow bias vs constant depth-bias Peter-Panning and shadow acne rig
topic_zh: Gruen 正弦法向偏移阴影偏置对比常数深度偏置脚底悬浮与掠射阴影摩尔纹
scope: Deterministic Holger Gruen (GDC 2011) algebraic sin-theta normal-offset shadow bias (delta_N = 0.5 * w_texel * sqrt(1 - (N.L)^2)) versus naive constant depth bias (Delta_z = 0.05m) and 32-ray trigonometric ray-plane intersection across 17 light incidence angle stations (theta in [5 deg, 85 deg]). No neural shadow denoising execution.

timing_note: Median of 7 alternating Node CPU runs after warmup. Algebraic sqrt(1 - (N.L)^2) normal-offset solver versus 32-ray acos/tan ray-plane intersection.

protocol.function: Δp = ½·w_texel·√(1 − (N·L)²)·N → Clears 0.2836 m Staircase at θ=80° With Only 0.0492 m Shift (0 Acne / 0 Peter-Pan)

robustness.name: Sampled 17 incidence angle stations clear the shadow-texel staircase without Peter-Panning or Shadow Acne

good_fit: Cascaded Shadow Maps (CSM), Virtual Shadow Maps (VSM), and spot-light shadow mapping in UE5, Unity, Frostbite, and Three.js
Eliminating grazing-angle shadow acne stripes (θ → 85°) without exploding depth bias via tan(θ) → ∞
Preserving tight contact shadows at character feet (θ → 0° where sin(θ) → 0) with zero Peter-Panning detachment
Computing sin(θ) = √(1 − (N·L)²) algebraically from N·L without calling acos() or sin()
not_for: Ray-traced hardware shadows (DXR RayQuery) where no discrete shadow-map texel grid exists (use rt_tMin + vertex normal offset)
Neural screen-space shadow synthesis or diffusion relighting
Infinitely thin two-sided foliage cards where normal N flips arbitrarily
